statement.p: Find constants a and b in the function f(x)=a x e^{b x} such that f(\frac{1}{4})=1 and the function has a local maximum at x=\frac{1}{4}.

static.solution:
f(x) = axe^{bx}, we have f'(x) = ae^{bx}+abxe^{bx}=ae^{bx}(1+bx). We want f(\frac{1}{4})=1, and since this is to be a maximum, we require f'(\frac{1}{4})=0. These conditions give
f(1/4) = \frac{a}{4} e^{b/4} = 1 and f'(1/4) = a e^{b/4}(1+b/4) = 0.
Since ae^{b/4} is non-zero, we can divide both sides of the second equation by ae^{b/4} to obtain 1 + \frac{b}{4} = 0. This implies b=-4. Plugging b=-4 into the first equation gives us a(\frac{1}{4})e^{-1}= 1, or a=4 e. How do we know we have a maximum at x=\frac{1}{4} and not a minimum? Since f'(x)=ae^{bx}(1+bx) = ()e^{-4 x}(1 - 4 x), and (4 e)e^{-4 x} is always positive, it follows that f'(x)>0 when x\lt \frac{1}{4} and f'(x)\lt 0 when x>\frac{1}{4}. Since f' is positive to the left of x=\frac{1}{4} and negative to the right of x = \frac{1}{4}, f(\frac{1}{4}) is a local maximum.
